text: Aperture, a critical element in camera lenses, significantly affects how much light enters the camera, thereby determining the camera's ability to capture images in low-light conditions. A wider aperture, typically indicated by a smaller f-number, allows more light to pass through. This increased light penetration is crucial in dim conditions as it enables the camera to maintain a desirable shutter speed and image quality. For instance, when the aperture is set at an f/1.8, more than twice as much light as with an f/4 can enter the camera sensor. This increased light capture capability is why wider apertures are favored by photographers seeking to achieve sharp, well-exposed images in less light.
summary: aperture affects light in cameras, wide apertures let more light in for low-light.
